The Detroit Pistons face the Giannis-led Miami Heat for the second time this season, but this is not the same Heat team Detroit beat 128-111 in the second game of the season. The Heat can get above .500 with a win after winning six of its past eight games, including the previous three in a row. The Heat are starting to understand how best to play around Giannis Antetokounmpo, especially Bam Adebayo. In the team’s most recent win, Bam and Giannis scored 37 points, and Davion Mitchell was able to support the big two with a 22-point, 17-assist effort.

The Pistons also had Jalen Duren the last time the two teams faced each other, and the big man is still out, and Detroit’s big man is still out recovering from a hamstring injury. Detroit’s big men have been an issue since Duren went down, and that could be an issue when going against both Bam and Giannis. Of course, the Pistons do have Cade Cunningham, and he has vaulted himself into a top-10 player in the NBA. Cunningham is coming off a career-high 52 points and an NBA-first 50-point, 10-assist, zero-turnover game. I’m not sure what he’ll be able to do for an encore, but if the Pistons don’t get decent efforts out of John Collins and Paul Reed, it might not matter.

pistons.headline: Pistons vs. Wizards final score: Cade makes history in double OT win
pistons.body:
WASHINGTON, DC - NOVEMBER 12: Cade Cunningham #2 of the Detroit Pistons celebrates against the Washington Wizards during the first overtime at Capital One Arena on November 12, 2026 in Washington, DC. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images

Cade Cunningham scored a career-high 52 points, and the Detroit Pistons needed every single one of them in a 144-140 victory in double overtime against the Washington Wizards. It was not just a career-best night for Cunningham, not just one of the top-5 scoring performances in Pistons history, it was the first game in NBA history that saw a player score 50 points, dish 11 assists, and commit zero turnovers.

Cunningham simply did it all. He scored 30 points in the fourth quarter and overtime. That includes a critical 3-pointer after the Wizards had crawled their way back into the lead in the first overtime on an Anthony Davis alley-oop dunk.

The Pistons trailed 130-127 and each team had traded misses. Cunningham calmly took the ball up the left side of the floor, took a pass from Ausar Thompson, and walked into a movement 3-pointer that hit nothing but net to tie the game. On the next possession, Cade swung the ball to Duncan Robinson for what felt like a game-sealing 3 with 9 seconds left, but a video review determined Duncan had approximately 1 milimeter of his foot on the line and changed it to a two.

The scoring barrage also included critical stretch in the fourth quarter where he scored eight points and assisted another to account for 11 of Detroit’s final 12 points of the fourth quarter. Cunningham also locked up Trae Young on defense with Detroit up 119-118 in the final 30 seconds of the fourth. He forced Young into the sideline, cut off any passing lane, deflected the ball, and forced shot clock violation.

Sadly, after Cade hit two free throws to make it a 3-point game, Young redeemed himself by hitting an off-balance three from 29 feet away to give us our two overtimes of fun.

Cunningham’s performance slightly overshadowed another notable feat — Ausar Thompson tallied his first career triple-double. He was aggressive on offense driving to the rim, and delivered crisp passes in narrow lanes to keep Detroit’s offense moving.

On a night where Cade scores 52 and Ausar gets a triple-double, how the heck was it so close to begin with? How does a game like that feature 20 lead changes and 13 ties? It was a weird game.

Alex Sarr was 12-of-14 from the floor and hit his first four threes of the night. He scored 30 points and was one of three Wizards to hit the 30-point threshold. Young scored a team-high 37 points, including a perfect 17-of-17 from the line. Anthony Davis scored 30 points and added 15 rebounds.

Honestly, Detroit’s biggest issue was the same issue they’ve had all season. Their bigs were dominated and DEtroit really misses Jalen Duren. Washington outscored Detroit in the paint and were outrebounded. The biggest issue was John Collins yet again. He was a minus-18 on the night and it felt like it was even worse.

Collins started the overtime period at center in place of Paul Reed, who was a plus-25, and promptly was the primary factor in Detroit giving up a 7-0 run to the Wizards right out of the gate. It was ugly. Come back soon, Jalen Duren.

Yeah, the Pistons might be missing Duren something fierce, but they have Cade Cunningham. And that’s enough.

Rarely have I been so interested in an immediate rematch as I am in tonight’s game, which sees the Detroit Pistons taking on the Washington Wizards for the second consecutive contest. The Pistons prevailed in Monday’s game 122-111. The game was also just dang weird. Anthony Davis played out of his mind, scoring 44 points in just 34 minutes. Rookie AJ Dybantsa also enjoyed the best game of his young pro career, scoring 21 and securing eight rebounds. Everyone else on the Wizards was pretty stinky.

Conversely, Cade Cunningham had one of the worst games of the season, and Detroit was really propelled by some excellent play from John Collins and Daniss Jenkins in a new-look starting lineup. Gone are the mismatched pair of Paul Reed and Collins sharing the floor. In is Collins as a center with room to operate and Jenkins as a secondary ball handler. It’ll be interesting to see if they build off that success or if it was temporary. If Detroit can get both Collins and Jenkins playing at a high level and a locked-in Cade, it could be a blowout. If instead the Wizards bounce back, it could get messy.

pistons.headline: Pistons vs. Wizards preview:  Round two against the Wizards
pistons.body:
The Pistons and Wizards play each other again, but it is after 3 days of rest for the Pistons and the day after a game for the Wizards because the NBA used Chat GPT to generate the schedule this year or something.  This will only be the Pistons 3rd game in the last 8 days and their 2nd game against the Wizards.

The Pistons were able to control Monday’s game from start-to-finish, but the game was a little closer than it should have been because they had no answer for Anthony Davis.  Davis finished the game with 44 points and only missed 5 shots total.

The Pistons will still be without Jalen Duren, so they once again may struggle to guard Anthony Davis.  But, as Monday proved, even if they can’t stop Davis, they can still win if they stop the rest of the team.

Game Vitals

Where:  Capital One Arena in Washington DC
When:  Thursday, November 12 at 7 pm EST
Watch:  Scripps Sports Network
Odds:  Pistons (-10.5)

Analysis

There isn’t a ton more to say about this matchup that wasn’t very evident in Monday’s game.  With Jalen Duren out, the Pistons have no solution to opposing big men with any kind of offensive skill that are over 6’10”.  It seems hyperbolic, but it really has been the case.  Paul Reed is undersized and John Collins is not a natural center.  Tolu Smith has the size to possibly keep up, but he has proven to be out of his element pretty much any time he has gotten playing time so far.

The Pistons did opt to start John Collins at center against the Wizards on Monday and it did work out offensively, as he had a season-high 24 points.  But, the aforementioned Anthony Davis was able to cruise to 44 points without much resistance.  Anthony Davis always seems to have his best games against the Pistons and I wouldn’t expect him to hit a couple threes every single night, but a lot of the offense he was able to generate was off of offensive rebound putbacks or shots over the undersized players guarding him.

Surprisingly, the Pistons were only outrebounded 46-45, but they were outrebounded 14-11 on the offensive glass.  If you watched the game, you could see the Pistons lack of size rear it’s head countless times.  It is just the current state of things and something the Pistons will have to manage as best as they can for the next two weeks while Jalen Duren is still out with his hamstring injury.

The Pistons benefitted heavily from poor games out of Alex Sarr and Kyshawn George, which George in particular has been arguably the Wizards 2nd best player this season.  Trae Young also had a poor night from beyond the arc where he shot 3-of-10.  Some of that is because of how good the Pistons perimeter defense is and if the Pistons can replicate that tonight, it doesn’t really matter if they have nobody to slow down Anthony Davis.

AJ Dybantsa was able to get going a bit on Monday as he scored 21 points on 8-of-17 shooting.  There were times where he looked overwhelmed, as he had 5 turnovers, but he showed why he was the number 1 pick and a building block for the Wizards.  The Pistons have perimeter players to slow him down, but the refs were very whistle-happy on Monday which helped Dybantsa get momentum on his drives to the basket since the Pistons were not able to be as physical.

One small point of concern has been the play of Cade Cunningham over the last few games.  He had arguably his best game of the season a little over a week ago against the Charlotte Hornets and since then has really struggled, especially from beyond the arc.  He is 1 for his last 19 from beyond the arc after being close to 40% through the first seven games of the season.

He is playing more off-ball and getting clean looks, they just aren’t falling right now.  Teams are obviously focusing their defense more on Cade, but a lot of the current issues are just due to not being able to hit his outside shots.  Hopefully that changes tonight.

Luckily, Daniss Jenkins has been able to step up the last couple nights as he had a career-high, 31 points against the Lakers on Sunday and then 22 points, 6 rebounds, and 8 assists on Monday while starting.  Given the success the Pistons had starting him along with John Collins at center, I would suspect that they roll out that starting lineup again.

There were some issues defensively, which I already touched on, but the offense was much better with Collins starting and more-importantly, it finally got John Collins going after his early-season struggles.

If the Pistons are able to replicate the game they played on Monday, they shouldn’t have a difficult time defeating the Wizards, but if they let one of the other players besides Anthony Davis get hot, the Wizards have a shot at the upset.

Lineups

Detroit Pistons (7-3):  Cade Cunningham, Daniss Jenkins, Duncan Robinson, Ausar Thompson, John Collins

Washington Wizards (4-8):  Trae Young, Kyshawn George, AJ Dybantsa, Anthony Davis, Alex Sarr

Question of the Day

Do you think there is a solution to the Pistons big-man struggles or do they just need to ride it out until Jalen Duren returns?

DETROIT, MI - NOVEMBER 9: John Collins #20 of the Detroit Pistons dunks the ball in the game against the Washington Wizards on November 9, 2026 at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit, Michigan. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Chris Schwegler/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

For those of you DBB sickos who care, I’m officially a married man! We had a spooky wedding on Halloween night and spent the past week in Cabo San Lucas for our honeymoon. We had a great time celebrating over the past week and a half!

Now we’re back to Pistons hoops.

JB Bickerstaff decided to mix up the starting lineup by starting John Collins at center. Paul Reed moved to the bench, and Daniss Jenkins was inserted into the starting lineup. Detroit started small with Duncan Robinson at the 3 and Ausar Thompson at the 4.

It proved to be the right idea early, as Collins was the leading scorer for Detroit after the first quarter with nine points. The Wizards took a 32-31 lead heading into the second, behind 12 points from Trae Young and 11 from Anthony Davis.

Detroit struggled to have an answer defensively for AD, and this was another game where Detroit missed Jalen Duren’s physicality and inside presence. Davis had 30 points and eight rebounds at the halfway point while only missing one of his 11 attempts. The Pistons put up 37 points in the quarter with five different players scoring more than seven points. Collins led the way with 15, Duncan had 14, and Cade had 11 as Detroit held a 68-58 lead.

The third quarter was all about Daniss Jenkins. Cade picked up his fifth foul halfway through the third, and DJ took the reins. He made Trae Young look like a traffic cone on defense as Jenkins went on to score 13 in the quarter. He consistently attacked Young, and Young never stood a chance. Detroit continued to extend their lead as they were up 103-87 heading into the fourth.

The fourth quarter was highlighted by two beautiful plays by Ebuka Okorie and Ausar Thompson.

First, watch Ausar find Okorie in transition as Okorie does his best Kyrie Irving impression:

AUSAR TO EBUKA WE ARE IN HEAVEN pic.twitter.com/jggv5WFEeC
— Rip Haminkton (@RedAlternates) November 10, 2026

Second, the Human Swiss Army knife blocks the 7-footer Alex Sarr on one end, then follows that up by directing traffic and finding an open DJ with a great bounce pass for a wide-open dunk:

Just let Ausar do everything pic.twitter.com/3nlVa0IHKi
— Rip Haminkton (@RedAlternates) November 10, 2026

The Pistons will continue to hope for a speedy recovery for Jalen Duren as they needed his inside physicality against Anthony Davis, who finished with 44 points and 13 rebounds while shooting 16-for-21 from the field. Detroit still managed to pull away with a 122-111 win behind three different players who scored 20+ points, despite none of them being Cade Cunningham.

John Collins, in his starting small-ball five role, led the way with 24 points and 10 rebounds, shooting 9-for-13 from the field. Both Daniss Jenkins and Duncan Robinson added 22 points each, and Jenkins led Detroit with eight assists. Your fun fact of the night: Robinson led the Pistons with seven free throw attempts. There has been a clear difference in his game this year as he looks to get to the line more often. Cunningham added 17 points and seven assists.

The Pistons improve to 7-3 on the season. Detroit’s home-and-home matchup with the Wizards continues as the Pistons will travel to Washington for Round 2 on Thursday night.

Go Stones.

pistons.headline: Pistons vs. Lakers: Austin Reaves pulls a Doncic to beat Detroit
pistons.body:
DETROIT, MI - NOVEMBER 8: Austin Reaves #15 of the Los Angeles Lakers drives to the basket during the game against the Detroit Pistons on November 8, 2026 at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit, Michigan. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Brian Sevald/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

Who needs Luka Doncic when you have the US equivalent from Newark, Arkansas, Austin Reaves? The Los Angeles Lakers guard scored a game-high 43 as his MVP-level teammate rested with a back injury, propelling LA past the Detroit Pistons 121-116.

Honestly, the game had no reason to be as close as it was in the end. The Lakers led 40-14 one basket into the second quarter courtesy of insane shotmaking (hitting 72% from the floor) and an insane amount of Pistons miscues, including having more turnovers (eight) than made baskets (six).

But the Pistons, being the Pistons, weren’t about to give up. While Detroit pulled within one point early in the fourth quarter, the Lakers led wire to wire. So while it was only marginally competitive from Detroit’s point of view, it was certainly an instructive game. Here are some of the things I learned:

1. Kevin Huerter

Kevin Huerter is going to be a critical component of the Pistons’ rotation this season. In a game where Detroit’s entire backcourt didn’t really show up to play (both Cade Cunningham and Duncan Robinson were largely no-shows until some fourth-quarter scoring), Huerter was by far the biggest bright spot for the Pistons.

It also happened to be his best game in a Detroit uniform. Huerter hit four three-pointers, scored 24 points overall, and added five rebounds, five assists, five blocks(?!) and two steals. Ever since the Pistons traded for him at the deadline last season, it was clear Huerter makes winning plays, and you were hoping he’d be able to combine that with rediscovering his 3-point shooting stroke from earlier in his career. The early returns indicate the shot might be back, as well as everything that goes with it. After tonight, he’s hitting 40% from deep this season.

2. John Collins and Paul Reed

Detroit’s starting front court simply does not work, and it will never work. For as long as Jalen Duren remains sidelined or off the floor this season, this is going to be a significant issue for the Pistons. Duren is ramping back up from a hamstring injury and will be out two more weeks. Detroit has been, and will continue to be able to weather that storm. But it ain’t pretty, and any additional time off from Duren will have me significantly worried.

Most will want to pin the blame on the newcomer John Collins, and he has certainly played worse than Reed, but I think it’s the combination that brings out the worst in both players. Each is the kind of big man that relies on the gravity from teammates that allows them to use their athleticism to create the chaos that makes them effective. With both of them on the floor, it’s two bouncy balls pinging around the floor with no semblance of a plan on how to actually get the ball to the rim. The defense is also bad, and the rebounding is even worse. It’s an ugly situation, and it was exacerbated tonight by both men getting out-physicaled by the behemoth seven-footer Walker Kessler. Kessler, the Lakers’ big offseason addition, had 12 points and 16 rebounds, including seven on the offensive end. The Lakers also dominated the Pistons in the paint, 58-46.

Again, the lion’s share of the blame goes to Collins. He’s been quite bad all season, and it’s getting less clear by the day how he’s going to turn it around and be a positive force for the Pistons. I don’t think he’s ever met a 50-50 ball he couldn’t surrender to the opposition. But the pathway to him playing well lies with sharing the floor with Duren. Get well soon, JD.

3. Austin Reaves

The Pistons were correct in trying to give Austin Reaves the bag this offseason. Detroit reportedly was ready to give the wing a max contract this offseason as the second scorer and potential missing piece in a Detroit Pistons title run. Once the Lakers believed the pending RFA had a max offer on the table, they quickly moved to get an agreement to sign him on the eve of free agency so he’d never hit the market.

Reaves was insane tonight. The degree of difficulty on his shots begged belief. He was able to create space, get balanced, and score at all three levels. It was a sight to behold, and he was by far the best player on the floor for either team tonight.

4. Daniss Jenkins

Daniss has that dog in him, especially under two scenarios: 1. There is an impending buzzer. 2. He feels like his team is getting punked. Jenkins was truly the other hero of the game behind Huerter. He hit yet another buzzer-beater tonight, and he scored a career-high 31 points. When the Pistons were down huge, Jenkins got that look in his eye, as if to say, “This is not going to happen.”

From there, Jenkins started firing away from deep, and he was hitting. In the end, he canned eight three-pointers. He was also the ONLY Pistons player to go to the free-throw line more than once in the game. Really, Jenkins is like a better version of Marcus Sasser. He’s got scoring in his blood, and he’s more of an off-guard than a point guard, despite being stuck in a point guard’s body. He’s got three inches on Sasser and better floor vision, so he’s better overall and can cosplay as a point guard better than Sass, but Jenkins works best in this Pistons lineup when he’s not running the offense.

4. The refs.

The referees love the Lakers. Nothing else needs to be said.

lions.headline: Detroit Lions Week 10 snap counts: Derrick Moore steps up after Hutchinson injury
lions.body:
Detroit Lions edge rusher Derrick Moore (8) celebrates a sack of Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis (not in the photo) during the second half at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co

In Week 10, the Detroit Lions moved to 7-2 after beating the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. The Lions dominated the game in every way, and while key injuries will certainly be prominent storylines, they shouldn’t overshadow the fact that Detroit is playing complementary football right now and looks like it can go head-to-head with anyone.

Let’s look at the snap counts from this game and see what they mean for the depth chart hierarchy and what we can ascertain moving forward.

Quarterback

Jared Goff: 61 (86%)

Josh Dobbs: 10 (14%)

With roughly seven minutes left in the fourth quarter and Detroit up 25 points, the Lions rested their starters, and Goff gave way to Dobbs for the final two possessions. Dobbs handed the ball off to the running backs six times, completed a first-down pass to Isaac TeSlaa, and the team went into victory formation for the final three plays.

Running back

Jahmyr Gibbs: 49 (69%)

Sione Vaki: 18 (25%) — 20 special teams snaps (71%)

Jacob Saylors: 6 (8%) — 20 (71%)

Gibbs once again put on a show, totaling 252 all-purpose yards and finding the end zone twice—despite only playing three-and-a-half quarters. Before the Lions pulled their starters, Gibbs saw over 80% of offensive snaps, with Vaki taking the RB2 snaps. Vaki also got the first three touches with the reserves, before giving way to Saylors, who closed out the game.

Wide receiver

Jameson Williams: 56 (79%)

Amon-Ra St. Brown: 47 (66%)

Isaac TeSlaa: 46 (65%)

Tay Martin: 11 (15%) — 20 (71%)

DeAndre Carter: 5 (7%) — 11 (39%)

The St. Brown storybook game will be talked about for years, and it played out even better than the NFL script writers could have hoped. His overall snaps were very similar to TeSlaa’s in this game, but context matters: St. Brown was pulled with the starters, and TeSlaa stepped into a WR1 role over the final 11 snaps, bringing things statistically closer than they were when the game was on the line. TeSlaa not only made a terrific acrobatic touchdown catch, again, but he also made the final catch of the game to seal the win.

Tight end

Sam LaPorta: 56 (79%)

Brock Wright: 39 (55%) — 9 (32%)

Tyler Conklin: 22 (31%)

Like the other skill-position groups, the tight end reserves saw a slight uptick in usage after the starters (including LaPorta) were pulled. Not much box-score production from this group—a combined 4 catches for 30 yards—but they were all vital contributors in the run game.

Offensive line

LG Christian Mahogany: 71 (100%) — 5 (18%)

RT Blake Miller: 71 (100%) — 5 (18%)

LT Penei Sewell: 61 (86%)

RG Tate Ratledge: 61 (86%) — 5 (18%)

C Juice Scruggs: 61 (100%) — 5 (18%)

LT/6th OL: Larry Borom: 10 (14%) — 5 (18%)

LG Miles Frazier: 10 (14%) — 5 (18%)

C Seth McLaughlin: 10 (14%)

C Cade Mays: Inactive (injury)

Absolute dominance up front throughout the day. PFF only faults the Lions for six (!) pressures allowed in this game, and the entire unit was mauling people in the run game. When the starters were pulled, Sewell was swapped out for Borum at LT, Frazier took over for Ratledge at RG, and McLaughlin got reps at center in place of Scruggs.

Interior defensive line

3T Alim McNeill: 42 (71%) — 2 (7%)

3T Skyler Gill-Howard: 31 (53%) — 3 (11%)

DT Tyleik Williams: 19 (32%) — 2 (7%)

DL Levi Onwuzurike: 17 (29%)

3T Mekhi Wingo: DNP (Inactive)

With the Patriots trailing by double digits most of the game, New England needed to pass a lot to stay competitive, and as a result, rookie Gill-Howard saw more snaps than Williams opposite McNeill. This situational rotation has worked all season, and the Lions shouldn’t feel the need to alter it.

EDGE

Rush End DJ Wonnum: 44 (75%) — 3 (11%)

Rush End Derrick Moore: 40 (68%) — 3 (11%)

Big End Tyler Lacy: 22 (37%) — 5 (18%)

EDGE Aidan Hutchinson: 9 (15%) — INJURY

Rush End Eric O’Neill: 7 (12%) — 11 (39%)

Big End Ahmed Hassanein: DNP (Inactive)

Following Hutchinson’s reported season-ending injury, the Lions turned to Wonnum and rookie Moore to step into larger roles. For Wonnum, it was a slight uptick from his typical starting reps, but Moore saw his opportunities increase sharply. Moore rewarded the Lions with four pressures and two sacks.

Moore is expected to see his role increase following Hutchinson’s injury, but in the two games where his opportunities increased due to injury, he accounted for nine pressures and four sacks, giving Lions fans some hope he can soften the blow of losing their All-Pro defensive end.

Linebacker

SAM Derrick Barnes: 59 (100%) — 1 (4%)

WILL/MIKE Malcolm Rodriguez: 34 (58%) — 2 (7%)

WILL/SAM Trevor Nowaske: 33 (56%) — 22 (79%)

MIKE K.J. Britt: 22 (37%) — 17 (61%)

MIKE Joe Bachie: 1 (2%) — 20 (71%)

WILL Owen Pappoe: 0 (0%) — 20 (71%)

WILL Amen Ogbongbemiga: DNP (Inactive)

Last week, their first without Jack Campbell in the lineup, the Lions leaned on Barnes and Rodriguez to play almost every snap, with Nowaske seeing about half the defensive snaps in a situational LB3 role. This week, Barnes and Nowaske’s roles stayed the same, but Rodriguez saw his snaps reduced in favor of Britt.

Rodriguez still played a significant role, but Britt’s inclusion is an interesting wrinkle to keep an eye on. Was Britt’s familiarity with the Patriots the catalyst for this decision (the Lions signed him off New England’s practice squad) or is this a sign of things to come? We’ll have to wait and see.

Cornerback

CB/NB Roger McCreary: 59 (100%) — 3 (11%)

CB Rock Ya-Sin: 55 (93%) — 1 (4%)

CB Khalil Dorsey: 21 (36%) — 18 (64%) — INJURED

CB Nick Whiteside: 7 (12%) — 3 (11%)

CB Ennis Rakestraw: 5 (8%) — 7 (25%)

CB D.J. Reed: Inactive (injury)

McCreary and Ya-Sin have settled in as starters with Reed out, and both are noticeably more comfortable with the defense now that they’ve scaled up man coverage. When Reed returns, look for Ya-Sin to step back into a CB3 role but still play a significant role in nickel sets.

Dorsey was injured in this game, and it’s unclear how that will affect him long-term, but it would be surprising to see the Lions turn to Whiteside or Rakestraw for more snaps, as both have struggled lately.

Safety

S Brian Branch: 59 (100%) — 1 (4%)

S Chuck Clark: 57 (97%) — 3 (11%)

DB Andre Cisco: 5 (8%) — 5 (18%)

DB Christian Izien: 1 (2%) — 16 (57%)

DB Keith Abney: DNP (Inactive)

Branch’s return has been felt in the secondary, and with him at a point where he doesn’t need to leave the field, the Lions have options at safety. Cisco played sparingly in his first game with the Lions, and it’s notable that he may have already passed Izien on the depth chart.

Specialists

K Jake Bates: 11 (39%)

P Jack Fox: 9 (32%)

LS Hogan Hatten: 9 (32%)

Bates had a kickoff out of bounds that he would like back, but otherwise it was a clean day for the group.

lions.headline: What’s next for the Detroit Lions’ defense after Aidan Hutchinson’s injury?
lions.body:
Detroit Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard reacts to a play Miami Dolphins during the first half at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co

The Detroit Lions are 7-2 and in the driver’s seat of the NFC North. They’re on a five-game winning streak; they’ve yet to lose a divisional game despite it being an extremely strong set of teams, and they are in the midst of playing their best football right now.

That’s all the good news. The bad news is that Aidan Hutchinson likely suffered a season-ending injury on Sunday, and it comes two weeks after the Lions lost another star captain, Jack Campbell, to injury.

On this week’s PODcast—where Erik Schlitt takes my place amongst the panel—we discuss everything that transpired during Sunday’s Detroit Lions vs. New England Patriots game in Munich, Germany. We talk about Amon-Ra St. Brown magical weekend, Jahmyr Gibbs’ continued path to MVP and Offensive Player of the Year consideration, and an inspired performance on the defense.

But for the second half of the show, the fellas mostly talk about the Hutchinson injury fallout. Who will need to step up on the defensive line? Who will get more opportunities? What kind of formations and schematic changes will defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard consider moving forward? And can the health and improvement of the secondary help mitigate some of the damage?

Check it all out on this week’s show. I’ll be back on Tuesday for the Midweek Mailbag podcast.

As always, you can catch the video version of the PODcast over on our YouTube and Twitch pages. Those versions include some between-segments banter about the other Week 10 games, and some thoughts on the NFC North. Please follow and subscribe to those channels, as well. We are SO CLOSE to 20,000 subscribers on YouTube.

lions.headline: Detroit Lions grades vs. Patriots: Team win offers hope despite Hutchinson injury
lions.body:
MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 15: Jahmyr Gibbs of Detroit Lions runs with the ball during the NFL match between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions at the Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Sebastian Widmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images

There was plenty to love about the Detroit Lions’ dominant win over the New England Patriots. And while Aidan Hutchinson’s injury may be the biggest headline from the Munich game, there was plenty from Allianz Arena that should keep Lions fans optimistic about the team moving forward.

Here is my Lions Week 10 report card and positional grades for Detroit’s 35-10 victory.

Quarterback: C+

Jared Goff threw two interceptions; both were his fault, and the second was an inexcusable decision that took points directly off the board. Because of those two plays alone, it feels like I can’t give him a grade above C+ in good faith.

But the truth is the rest of his day was pretty dang good. I thought he navigated the pocket well, especially on his 50-yard pass to Jahmyr Gibbs. He didn’t make a ton of downfield throws or display any jaw-dropping plays, but he was very efficient, finishing with an electric 9.8 yards per attempt and a 101.9 passer rating.

Running backs: A+

Jahmyr Gibbs was incredible all freakin’ day. He finished with 252 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns. The Patriots couldn’t handle his speed, his change-of-direction, or his strength. What was even better about his performance than normal is that the negative plays were almost completely non-existent. He had just one touch that went for negative yards, and only a couple more were stopped for zero yards.

Sione Vaki was very efficient, too, earning 28 yards on just six carries (4.7 YPC).

Overall, the Lions produced an impressive 55% success rate and +0.21 EPA/play on running plays vs. the Patriots. For comparison’s sake, the Patriots were allowing just a 36.9 success rate going into this game and had produced a negative EPA/run.

Tight ends: B

I was a little disappointed with Sam LaPorta’s play as a receiver. He didn’t create much separation against the Patriots’ defenders, and he had a touchdown grab knocked out of his hands. He finished with just a single catch for 16 yards on four targets.

However, the Lions used a ton of tight ends against the Patriots in the running game, and that played a significant role in Detroit controlling the line of scrimmage. LaPorta (26), Brock Wright (29), and Tyler Conklin (17) all logged over 15 run-blocking snaps on the day.

Wide receivers: A+

Amon-Ra St. Brown was seemingly unstoppable on Sunday. It was going to take the entire country of Germany to stop him on both of his long catch-and-run touchdowns, and they certainly weren’t going to do that against their most beloved NFL player.

Jameson Williams’ day shouldn’t be overlooked, either. He caught four passes for 50 yards, including an impressive toe-tapping catch on the sidelines. Even Isaac TeSlaa got in on the fun with a highlight-reel touchdown grab.

This unit lived up to its full potential for the first time in several weeks.

Offensive line: A-

Outside of some early pass protection issues, the Lions’ offensive line was nails in Munich. They were getting significant push in the run game, and after settling down, they helped Jared Goff breathe comfortably in the pocket.

When the offensive line plays this well, the Lions’ entire offense is as close to unstoppable as we’ve seen.

Defensive line: A-

While the Lions’ pressure was inconsistent at times without Aidan Hutchinson in the lineup, they still gave the Patriots hell for most of the game. In the run game, the Patriots were unable to do anything. Their running backs combined for 17 carries, 31 yards, and just 1.8 yards per carry.

The pass rush generated five total sacks, six quarterback hits, and over a 50 percent pressure rate:

Pressure was a problem again for the Patriots today

Lions pressured them on 51% of plays (up from 46% season rate, 2nd highest in the NFL).

*This is the 5th time this season NE has allowed a pressure on 50% or more of dropbacks*

Data: @SumerSports
— Lindsay Rhodes (@lindsay_rhodes) November 15, 2026

It will be tough to maintain that without Hutchinson and against a better offensive line, but Derrick Moore, Alim McNeill, DJ Wonnum, and Skyler Gill-Howard have all played some pretty sound football, and all were disruptive on Sunday.

Linebackers: B

The linebackers deserve a lot of praise for Detroit’s stout run defense, but they were a bit of a liability in the pass game again. It didn’t end up costing the Lions too much in this game, because once Drake Maye went down, it looked like Tommy DeVito just didn’t see the field very well. But coverage against tight ends and running backs continues to be a bit of an issue.

Still, this defense continues to play good football without its field general at MIKE linebacker, and that means something.

Secondary: A-

I thought the safety play was fantastic on Sunday. Brian Branch was all over the place in the run game and the pass game. Chuck Clark flipped a couple Patriots and made the receiving corps pay for every DeVito murderball.

I can’t give them an A, though, because of a couple of stupid and costly pass interference flags. It wasn’t a great game for Ennis Rakestraw—who also missed a key tackle—nor Nick Whiteside. But the good news is the top corners in this game—Rock Ya-Sin and Roger McCreary were very, very good. Or, as Dan Campbell said:

“I thought the back end played outstanding,” Campbell said. “We played some sticky coverage today, bought us a little bit of time.”

Special teams: B

Nothing too notable from this group on Sunday. The return team didn’t look particularly good, but coverage was good on both punt and kickoff. Jake Bates is still perfect when Jack Fox isn’t blocking his kicks. He did put a kickoff out of bounds and a touchback in the end zone.

Coaching: A

This was a tough week for both coaches. Flying across the globe, adjusting to a time zone six hours away, and dealing with all of the crazy logistics of getting ready for Sunday is not easy. It’s clear one team was way more prepared than the other.

On top of that, Lions offensive coordinator Drew Petzing is really starting to come into his own, building plays off of previous plays, and seemingly having the right call in the right moment more often than not. As he hits his stride, the Lions offense can carry them a long way.

But don’t sleep on the defensive coaching, either. Kelvin Sheppard has had to deal with two emotionally draining injuries to two of their best players. Yet through a heavy rotation at every level of the defense, things have never looked more steady and controlled. Say what you will, facing a beat-up Patriots offense with a backup quarterback leading most of Sunday afternoon, but Detroit used to get beat up by backups all the time. The defense finally feels like it’s coming together.

lions.headline: Discussion: Are you confident in the Detroit Lions defense without Aidan Hutchinson?
lions.body:
MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 15: Aidan Hutchinson of Detroit Lions goes down with an injury while celebrating getting a sack during the NFL match between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions at the Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Sebastian Widmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images

The Pyrrhic victories are unfortunately mounting for the Detroit Lions.

Despite winning five games in a row, they have lost two irreplaceable parts of their team. The Lions have now lost two cornerstone pieces of their defense over the last three weeks. Jack Campbell suffered a scary neck injury and will be sidelined for an unknown period of time. Against the New England Patriots in Munich, the Lions lost yet another heartbeat of their defense. Aidan Hutchinson suffered a serious knee injury that will likely sideline him for the rest of the 2026 season—and perhaps into the 2027 season as well.

The impact Hutchinson has on this team is difficult to quantify. For a team built on grit, Hutchinson exemplified that to a tee. Without Hutchinson, can the Lions defense continue to play at a high level?

Today’s Question of the Day is:

Are you confident in the Detroit Lions defense without Aidan Hutchinson?

My answer: I am cautiously optimistic.

Few teams boast a pass rusher like Hutchinson, and he was by far the most potent edge on the Lions’ roster. Hutchinson will finish the season with 52 pressures per PFF, while the next-closest defender is Alim McNeill (36) and the next-closest edge is DJ Wonnum (18)—that’s a significant gap. Without question, the Lions are in a far worse position than they were entering the week. The ceiling for the Lions to be a great defense is gone, in my opinion.

However, I think the floor is still intact.

When the Lions lost Hutchinson back in 2024, their defense was ill-equipped to handle it. The pass rushing depth was largely just Josh Paschal and Al-Quadin Muhammad and The Lions had to make a deadline deal to acquire Za’Darius Smith. They lost Alim McNeill to a torn ACL in Week 15. By the time they rolled into the postseason, their pass rush was limited. This limitation put a lot of pressure on the secondary, and the defense wound up allowing 45 points to the Commanders. This, in turn, forced the offense to be perfect, and on a day when Jared Goff threw three interceptions, it was not.

I think the rest of 2026 will be tough sledding for the defense, but the Lions have some options. For one, Wonnum has been playing very well this season. He is not the game-wrecker that Hutchinson is, but he is a steady presence capable of sound run defense and pass rush. Secondly, rookie Derrick Moore is coming into his own of late, now having four sacks in two games. Refining his skillset is still a priority for him, but it’s not hard to see the potential with him. It might be earlier than expected, but he now has to step into a sizable role on defense.

The Lions also have McNeill playing at an All-Pro level, while Tyleik Williams is quietly entrenching himself as a menace up the middle. Sprinkle in guys like Tyler Lacy (another underappreciated player) and Skyler Gill-Howard (the pass-rushing rookie tackle), and the Lions not only have more talent on the defensive line than in 2024, but also more flexibility.

The loss of Hutchinson will put more pressure on the secondary to step up. The secondary has been balling as of late, but there will be questions about whether that is a mirage or not. Over the last five games, the defense has played the hapless Arizona Cardinals, the inconsistent Green Bay Packers, the formerly-hapless Minnesota Vikings, the hapless Miami Dolphins, and the Drake Maye-less New England Patriots. You can only play the opponent on the schedule, but concerns about the authenticity of this defensive turnaround are certainly justified—are they actually good now or just benefitting from weak and misfortunate opponents? If the Lions can put up a great defensive showing versus the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving, then you can squash some of my doubts.

What makes me encouraged about the secondary is that they look invigorated. They are intercepting passes. They are batting away balls. They are (mostly) limiting the explosive plays. Whereas the defense looked lost to start the season, they are playing with far more confidence at this point. Getting Brian Branch was certainly a catalyst, and if the Lions can add Kerby Joseph to the mix as well, then the defensive back group suddenly looks far more capable

You cannot replace a player like Hutchinson. You will struggle to even recreate him in the aggregate. He is a rarity amongst NFL players, a player with a high level of talent and the motor to back it up. However, I think that the Lions have enough pieces on their defense to weather the storm. If they can be a good defense, that might be enough when paired with this potent offense.

Do you have faith in this defense without Hutchinson? Let us know in the comments below.

lions.headline: 14 winners, 3 losers from Detroit Lions’ win over the New England Patriots
lions.body:
MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 15: Amon-Ra St. Brown of Detroit Lions celebrates scoring his team's fourth touchdown with teammates during the NFL match between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions at the Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Sebastian Widmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images

Guten tag, Detroit Lions fans.

The Munich road trip comes to a close with a victory, as the Lions beat the schnitzel out of the New England Patriots on Sunday. In perhaps their most complete game of the season, the offense was nigh unstoppable while the defense silenced the entire New England arsenal. The final score ended as 35-10, but it could have been far worse for the Patriots.

Two injuries were at the forefront of this game—both happening on the same play. Quarterback Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury after being tackled by Aidan Hutchinson on a sack. The Patriots offense was paltry under backup Tommy DeVito and would not score until late in the fourth quarter. Hutchinson, meanwhile, suffered an injury while celebrating that very sack. He too did not return and is likely done for the season.

The season-ending Hutchinson injury looms large for Detroit, but we should at least appreciate the team-wide performance in this beatdown.

Note: The label of “loser” is used to evaluate and contrast in-game performance and is not an indictment of a player’s ability, value, or character. The term is not intended to be disrespectful in nature.

Winner: Jahmyr Gibbs, RB

I am running out of words to describe Jahmyr Gibbs, so instead, I will use only three: most valuable player. There is no other way to illustrate Gibbs’ impact on the Lions right now. He gets the most out of every play—give him an inch and he takes a mile. Gibbs finished with 22 carries for 153 yards and two touchdowns while adding seven catches for 99 yards. He was arguably more impressive than those numbers indicate, too. Gibbs looks untouchable. The offensive line, receivers, and tight ends were moving people ahead of him, but Gibbs’ ability to turn any play into a big gain was a game-changer.

We are truly witnessing something special.

Winner: Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR

Can you tell that St. Brown wanted to make the most of his first game in Germany?

The Lions star receiver of German ancestry put on a clinic in Munich, rattling off chunk play after chunk play. He ended the day with just four catches, but he turned those into 98 yards and two touchdowns. The first was a brilliant 56-yarder in which he juked most of the Patriots defense. The second was just 28 yards, but the final eight of those were a rugby scrum powered by will, determination, and a handful of Lions pushing behind him.

For most teams, a performance like this would be the highlight of the game. For the Lions, it’s just another day at the office. They are so fortunate to have players like St. Brown and Gibbs playing at an All-Pro level on a weekly basis.

Winners: Roger McCreary and Rock Ya-Sin, CBs

The absence of Drake Maye definitely benefitted the Lions defense, but that should not detract from the sticky coverage provided by Ya-Sin and McCreary. The Patriots only had 90 passing yards on the day as A.J. Brown and the other Patriot pass catchers were smothered by the Lions defensive backs. McCreary got his first interception of the season and was phenomenal in coverage, recording two passes defended and zero explosives allowed. Ya-Sin, after struggling to start the season, has found his footing of late. He also had a pass defended and, per PFF, did not allow a catch on three targets.

Early on in year, losing D.J. Reed would have been a death sentence for the Lions defense, but Ya-Sin and McCreary have stepped up and the Lions have weathered the storm.

Winner: Offensive line

A week after the offensive line got bullied by the Miami Dolphins, they got their act together against the Patriots. Gibbs’ shined on Sunday, but he never reaches that level without capable blocking ahead of him. All five of the starters were blasting through the Patriots front seven, generating plenty of rushing lanes for Gibbs to showcase his speed and agility. The return of Christian Mahogany surely impacted this blocking turnaround—hopefully the disciplinary penalty he received last week sticks going forward. Jared Goff was sacked twice on the day, but both were arguably coverage sacks. Aside from a pair of penalties (one on Blake Miller, one on Tate Ratledge), there was very little to criticize from the blocking up front.

Winner: Derrick Moore, DE

Are we witnessing Moore’s rookie breakout? It was a slow start to his season, but he is coming into his own lately. Moore had a pair of sacks against the Patriots and now has four sacks across his last two games. He has flashed the full toolkit—speed, bend, power, finesse, and motor. Consistency is still the name of the game for Moore’s development, particularly in run defense, but his pass rush prowess over the last month has been encouraging. His rapid development becomes even more paramount with Aidan Hutchinson missing extensive time due to his injury.

Winner: Derrick Barnes, LB

I thought that this was arguably Barnes’ best game of the season. Barnes was a menace in run defense, racking up a team-leading seven tackles and three run stops per PFF. As a pass rusher, Barnes flashed some serious closing speed, pressuring the Patriots quarterbacks on multiple occasions. Most encouraging of all, Barnes looked capable in coverage—normally his weakness. The Patriots had little success with their tight ends and running backs and Barnes was a key reason why. He never looked lost in coverage and shadowed his man effectively.

The Lions needed Barnes to step up after Jack Campbell’s injury, and performances like these do a lot to instill confidence in the linebacking corps going forward.

Quick hits:

Winner: Drew Petzing, OC
Petzing was on fire on Sunday. The Lions got a lot of great performances on offense, but none of them happen without the right play call at the right time. Nearly everything Detroit threw at New England worked. Petzing deserves to be in the conversation for best offensive coordinator in the league.

Winner: Sione Vaki, RB
Vaki only had a limited number of touches before garbage time (six carries for 28 yards and one catch for 17 yards), but he continues to make impactful plays when called upon. He also had a brilliant pass block that enabled Goff to hit St. Brown for his 56-yard touchdown. Even if Isiah Pacheco returns this season, Vaki has cemented his spot as a dependable RB2.

Loser: Sam LaPorta, TE
He and Brock Wright are doing well as blockers, especially with the sidecar formation, but his lack of impact as a receiver (one catch for 16 yards) is concerning. Over the last four games, he has just nine catches for 99 yards.

Winner: Alim McNeill, DT
Another week with a sack for McNeill. Few defensive tackles in the league have his combination of run stopping and pass rush.

Winner: DJ Wonnum, DE
Moore finished with two sacks, but Wonnum was a solid contributor as well. He had a sack of his own along with multiple pressures. Given his ability as a pass rusher and run defender, he will be relied upon as an every-down player with Hutchinson missing time.

Winner: Brian Branch, S
Branch has unquestionably played a massive part in the Lions’ defensive turnaround. His ability in coverage and run defense are instrumental to the entire defense succeeding. He had two passes defended and three run stops on Sunday.

Losers: Ennis Rakestraw and Nick Whiteside, CB
Rakestraw only played a few snaps but made the least of them. He gave up a catch to Hunter Henry after a poor tackling attempt. On the ensuing drive, he committed a pass interference—a 30-yard penalty that nearly outpaced the Patriots offense. As for Whiteside, he got called for pass interference late in the game that helped facilitate a Patriots touchdown. With Ya-Sin and McCreary playing well, Rakestraw will likely stay limited to reserve duties and Whiteside might get shuttled back to the practice squad.

Winner: Isaac TeSlaa, WR
TeSlaa is still only catching a pass or two per game, but he makes the most them. His touchdown grab was a brilliant acrobatic catch. When you factor in his blocking, this was a perfect performance for a tertiary option on offense.

Winner: K.J. Britt, LB
Not only was Britt surprisingly active on defense (22 snaps per PFF), he was surprisingly solid. His coverage and run defense were both stout. The Lions have been rotating Malcolm Rodriguez and Trevor Nowaske behind Barnes, but now Britt also enters the fray as a depth option.

lions.headline: Report: Aidan Hutchinson out for season after injury during celebration
lions.body:
MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 15: Aidan Hutchinson of Detroit Lions celebrates sacking Drake Maye of New England Patriots before going down with an injury caused by celebrating during the NFL match between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions at the Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Adam Pretty/Getty Images) | Getty Images

Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson made a huge play on the opening drive in Munich to end the Patriots’ attack with a sack. But what he did afterward may be the story of the game. Jumping into the air in celebration, Hutchinson landed on his feet, only to immediately crumple to the ground with an injury. After down on the field for a couple of minutes, Hutchinson was able to walk to the sideline on his own and into the blue tent.

Aidan Hutchinson just got hurt celebrating a sack pic.twitter.com/bz1CY4G4Av
— Arye Pulli (@AryePulliNFL) November 15, 2026

After several minutes in the blue tent, Hutchinson walked gingerly to the locker room.

Hutchinson is obviously one of the most important players on the Lions, currently leading the entire NFL in pressures through nine weeks. He has 6.0 sacks on the season. Hutchinson is also just two years removed from a broken leg injury that shortened his 2024 season.

UPDATE: The injury is feared to be significant and season-ending, per several reports:

Lions star DE Aidan Hutchinson suffered a significant knee injury, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports.

Imaging in Munich confirmed the injury to Hutchinson, whose right knee buckled as he celebrated a sack against the Patriots. He’s out for the season. pic.twitter.com/HiQqKghQew
— Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 15, 2026

UPDATE: The Lions listed Hutchinson as QUESTIONABLE to return with a knee injury.

#Lions Injury Update:

EDGE Aidan Hutchinson, Knee, Questionable
— Detroit Lions PR (@LionsPR) November 15, 2026

UPDATE 2: Hutchinson was officially downgraded to OUT in the second half.

UPDATE 3: Dan Campbell did not offer any sort of definitive update on Hutchinson after the game, only noting that he was happy with how the team responded to his injury, and they’ll need to step up if Hutchinson’s injury is long term.

For a full transcript on what Campbell said, check out this post on what the Lions coach had to say about Hutchinson’s injury.

lions.headline: Everything Dan Campbell said about Aidan Hutchinson’s injury
lions.body:
MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 15: Aidan Hutchinson of Detroit Lions receives medical attention after going down with an injury while celebrating getting a sack during the NFL match between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions at the Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Adam Pretty/Getty Images) | Getty Images

We still don’t have a firm update on Aidan Hutchinson after he suffered an injury celebrating a first-down sack in the Detroit Lions’ Week 10 win over the New England Patriots. However, Lions coach Dan Campbell was asked several questions about the situation, even though he didn’t provide an exactly diagnosis.

UPDATE: There are now reports that Hutchinson’s injury is feared to be season-ending.

What’s the latest update on Aidan Huthcinson?

Hutchinson was initially listed as questionable with a knee injury, then downgraded to out in the second half. Campbell would not offer up any additional information.

“Nothing new. We’ll know more when we get back in the States,” Campbell said. “But anytime you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate that he is, he’s a captain of ours, that doesn’t make things easy. But I thought guys stepped up in his wake and showed up for us today and helped us out.”

Does Hutchinson’s injury put a damper on the win over the Patriots?

Campbell:

“Anytime you lose a player like that and you don’t know the entirety of it–but knowing Hutch for who he is. It’s like he doesn’t stay down long. It does, it hurts a little bit, but as far as this game was concerned our guys stepped up and finished. We stayed strong. This is the second time this has happened—our guys have responded in a tough situation and didn’t bat an eye. Just went back to work, and that’s not easy to do. But, no, certainly you don’t want to know that a player like that is down.”

What kind of depth do the Lions have?

Detroit managed to create four more sacks on the day after Hutchinson’s injury—two by rookie Derrick Moore, one from Alim McNeill, and one from DJ Wonnum. Campbell expressed confidence in the Lions’ group of pass rushers, regardless of what Hutchinson’s ultimate diagnosis is.

“We like ‘em,” Campbell said. “That’s why we applied them where we did. And I know this, Derrick Moore gets better every game. The more reps he gets, he gets better. It was good to get Wonnum back today. We know what Mac [McNeill] is, Sky(ler Gill-Howard). So can Tyleik (Williams). And all those guys, even Levi (Onwuzurike), (Tyler) Lacy, they play a different flavor, but they push the pocket, they got movement. But I think the important thing is, man, we knew we had to do to get out of this game with a win. We had to play really good defense.

“And I really thought the back end played outstanding. We played some stick coverage today […] We’re improving. We gotta go. We gotta go. We’ll see where Hutch is at, but we’ve gotta step up now. We need some guys to really step up—and if that is the case (with a serious Hutchinson injury), fill that role.”

lions.headline: 5 takeaways from Detroit Lions’ dominant 35-10 win over New England Patriots
lions.body:
MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 15: Amon-Ra St. Brown of Detroit Lions celebrates scoring his team's first touchdown with teammates Christian Mahogany and Isaac TeSlaa during the NFL match between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions at the Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Adam Pretty/Getty Images) | Getty Images

Early-morning football today as the Detroit Lions faced the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. Detroit hasn’t played overseas since 2015, and they did a lot better than back then. Instead of losing 45-10, Detroit came out on top, winning 35-10, improving to 7-2. They’re back up above .500 overseas, improving to 2-1 in that regard.

Here are my five takeaways from the Lions’ 35-10 beatdown against the Patriots.

Aidan Hutchinson gives Lions fans PTSD

Let’s get the biggest negative out of the way. EDGE Aidan Hutchinson suffered a knee injury early in the game while celebrating after sacking Patriots quarterback Drake Maye. It reminded multiple Lions fans of when former linebacker Stephon Tulluch got injured after celebrating as well. Hutchinson didn’t return after it was labeled a knee injury.

After the game, Lions head coach Dan Campbell didn’t have an update on Hutchinson.

No Hutch? No problem for the Lions’ pass rush

Unlike 2024, the Lions defensive line can still generate pressure without its best player, Hutchinson. Even without him, the line came away with three sacks. Team sack leader EDGE DJ Wonnum got a sack in his return after missing a game due to a concussion. Defensive tackle Alim McNeill is continuing to have a solid season and also got a sack.

With Hutchinson out, rookie EDGE Derrick Moore saw more playing time and stepped up, essentially replacing one Wolverine with another. Moore didn’t just get one sack, but he got two. Back-to-back games with multiple sacks is a good look for the rookie, who has needed time to adjust to the NFL.

A third-down SACK for Derrick Moore!! pic.twitter.com/xfk49zju6f
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 15, 2026

The secondary helped out too, giving the defensive line time to get to either quarterback. This team has depth along that defensive line, which is why it can still be a problem even without Hutchinson. Hutchinson is certainly an important piece, but good teams can survive when their stars go down, and this unit didn’t fold without him this morning.

Amon-Ra St. Brown made the most of his return to Germany

All week, Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown was talked about in his return to Germany. He has family ties and spent summers in the country, so he was excited to play football in front of their fans. Quickly, St. Brown balled out and made a huge play, scoring the first touchdown and giving Detroit the lead they would never give back.

AMON-RA ST. BROWN 56-YARD TOUCHDOWN IN GERMANY

NEvsDET on FOX/FOX One
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/47fPY2mHzx
— NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026

St. Brown wasn’t done; he got another touchdown on a great play call by Lions offensive coordinator Drew Petzing. St. Brown was due to have a big game in front of the German fans, and the Lions made sure of it. St. Brown finished with four catches for 98 yards and two touchdowns.

Touchdown No. 2 for Germany's own Amon-Ra St. Brown ✅🇩🇪 pic.twitter.com/eAeQ2KijiL
— St. Brown Podcast (@StBrownPodcast) November 15, 2026

Gibbs helping case for MVP

While St. Brown dominated through the air, running back Jahmyr Gibbs dominated on the ground and through the air. New England has a strong run defense, allowing an average of 96.7 yards entering Sunday, ninth-lowest in the NFL. Detroit got left guard Christian Mahogany back after suffering an in-team suspension, and his return helped Gibbs too. All that said, Gibbs finished with 22 carries for 153 yards, two rushing touchdowns, and seven catches for 99 yards.

Jahmyr Gibbs has 171 yards in the 1st half (93 rushing yards, 78 receiving yards)

That is the most in a 1st half in a game this season and tied for 2nd in a game since 2022, @SumerSports
— Shawn Syed (@SyedSchemes) November 15, 2026

It’s great to see Gibbs play well against a respectable run defense. He’s the best player in the NFL trying to win the MVP trophy who isn’t a quarterback. He’s been dominant this season, with few poor performances, and when he has a solid game, he goes off. This offense was humming, and he was a big factor in it. He deserves the biggest push for the MVP trophy in December, when the focus starts to shift toward awards.

Jared Goff had an up-and-down performance

Despite Gibbs playing well and St. Brown scoring multiple times, quarterback Jared Goff had an up-and-down performance. While he threw for 303 yards and three touchdowns, he threw two interceptions, his first multi-interception game of the year. Goff was in his bag at times, throwing great passes to St. Brown, Jameson Williams, and Gibbs. But Goff also made some head-scratching errant throws.

The first interception came off a bad throw to a covered St. Brown, where Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez picked it off as St. Brown fell. Even if St. Brown didn’t fall, he was still covered, and it was the first interception this year solely on Goff. He wasn’t hit as he threw it, and the receiver falling wasn’t a factor.

His second interception was even worse, as Detroit was inside the five on third down with less than 10 seconds left in the first half, a situation where you either score or throw the ball away. Goff instead threw a ball into coverage, where it was picked off, and instead of at least getting a field goal on the drive, the Lions came away empty-handed. Goff had some good throws and some bad ones, a roller coaster game that, luckily, the good outweighed the bad. If Gibbs and the defense didn’t play as well as they did, this game could’ve been closer.

michigan.headline: 3 Michigan Football players expected to be out for the season due to injuries
michigan.body:
EUGENE, OR - NOVEMBER 14: JJ Buchanan #6 of the Michigan Wolverines drops the pass during the 1st half of a game between the Michigan Wolverines and Oregon Ducks at Autzen Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Eugene, Oregon. (Photo by Al Sermeno/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images

Michigan Football head coach Kyle Whittingham spoke to the media on Monday and revealed that star wide receiver JJ Buchanan (shoulder), and offensive linemen Blake Frazier (leg) and Andrew Sprague (undisclosed) are expected to be out of the rest of the year.

With only two games remaining in the regular season, Michigan will be without three significant contributors on the offensive side of the ball. Frazier and Buchanan went down with injuries in consecutive weeks, while Sprague hasn’t played since Week 2.

Buchanan went down with a left shoulder injury in the first half of a 31-7 loss against the Oregon Ducks on Saturday. He was reportedly transported to a local hospital for a re-evaluation. Now, his first season at Michigan is over.

“Unfortunately, we lost him and it looks like he’s probably going to be out for the season,” Whittingham told the media. “That’s very disappointing. It’s not 100 percent but that’s what it’s looking like after the follow up.”

The sophomore wide receiver leads the team with 646 receiving yards and five touchdowns on 40 receptions.

Meanwhile, Frazier started the first eight games of the season before getting hurt against the Michigan State Spartans. The Michigan offensive tackle started 16 games the last two seasons and has lined up all over the offensive line.

Sprague has missed every game since Week 2 with an undisclosed injury and is now officially out for the rest of this year. The details of Sprague’s injury haven’t been made public, but center Jake Guarnera previously said he didn’t leave the team after rumors went wild on social media at the time.

“Probably not (going to play again),” Whitingham said when asked if Frazier or Sprague could return this year. “I guess Andrew is out for certain and Blake would be a long shot to play. It’s unfortunate because they are two really good players.”

The Wolverines are expected to be without Buchanan, Frazier and Sprague as the regular season wraps up against the UCLA Bruins on Saturday before traveling to face the Ohio State Buckeyes in The Game on Nov. 28.

michigan.headline: Big Ten Football Power Rankings narrows in on the correct order
michigan.body:
BLOOMINGTON, IN - NOVEMBER 14: Indiana Hoosiers running back Lee Beebe Jr. (29) with he stiff arm to USC Trojans safety Prophet Brown (16) in the first half of play during a college football game between the USC Trojans vs the Indiana Hoosiers on November 14, 2026 at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, IN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images

Indiana picked up a huge win and crushed USC’s hopes and dreams of a CFP berth. Iowa and UCLA continued to chug along, while Wisconsin and Minnesota suffered ugly defeats.

There are now just two weeks left in the regular season. Here are our latest Big Ten Power Rankings.

10. Wisconsin Badgers: 6-4, Lost to Maryland, 24-21, LW: 7

Oof. That’s a bad loss. Just a month after Luke Fickell picked up the biggest win of his tenure vs USC, he arguably suffered his worst defeat. Losing to hapless Maryland at this stage in the season with an interim coach is as bad as it gets. It might even be enough to put him back on the hot seat.

9. Washington Huskies: 6-4, Def. Michigan State, 21-14, LW: 11

Jedd Fisch’s Huskies have reached bowl eligibility, as they have won three of their last four. They now host Indiana in a game in which a majority of the Big Ten will be rooting for the Huskies, as several teams need Indiana to lose in order to have a chance at reaching the Big Ten Championship.

8. Illinois Fighting Illini: 6-4, Lost to UCLA, 22-14, LW: 9

Illinois couldn’t get the job done on Friday night in Los Angeles. However, the Fighting Illini defense played an inspired game. Illinois only trailed 12-7 heading into the fourth quarter despite playing in a rain-soaked Rose Bowl. Bret Bielema’s squad rounds out the season with senior night against Iowa and a trip to Evanston to face Northwestern.

7. Northwestern Wildcats: 6-4, Lost to Ohio State, 28-19, LW: 8

Despite losing, Northwestern moves up a spot after being competitive with Ohio State despite a rash of injuries. At one point this season, the Wildcats looked like they had a chance to pull off the impossible and make the CFP. While those dreams are certainly dead now, bowl eligibility is still a successful season in Evanston.

6. Ohio State Buckeyes: 7-3, Def. Northwestern, 28-19, LW: 6

Ohio State got back in the win column against Northwestern, but it was far from convincing. The Wildcats were without their starting quarterback and still managed to move the ball. Jeremiah Smith was too much in the end, allowing the Buckeyes to technically stay alive for the CFP, but it would require a miracle.

5. USC Trojans: 7-3, Lost to Indiana, 27-13, LW: 5

We’ve reached the point in the season where it’s hard to drop teams in the rankings even despite losses. The Trojans suffered a heartbreaking loss to Indiana in a game they had to have to keep their CFP hopes alive. However, teams 7-10 in our power rankings last week also lost and No. 6 Ohio State now has the same record as USC, but the Trojans won the head-to-head.

4. Oregon Ducks: 7-3, Def. Michigan, 31-7, LW: 4

If there was any doubt that quarterback Dylan Raiola had turned the corner, Saturday’s game proved it. Raiola threw for 341 yards and four touchdowns against a very good Michigan defense. The Ducks will need some help, but their CFP hopes aren’t dead yet.

3. Iowa Hawkeyes: 8-2, Def. Purdue, 28-7, LW: 3

Iowa won a third consecutive game in a convincing rout over Purdue. Iowa only has a trip to Illinois and home game with Nebraska left on the schedule. If Indiana and UCLA both win out, Iowa would finish 10-2 with no Big Ten Championship appearance. Is that good enough for the CFP? Time will tell.

2. Indiana Hoosiers: 9-1, Def. USC, 27-13, LW: 2

Indiana had the most impressive win of the weekend in the conference, ending Lincoln Riley’s CFP hopes. I seriously contemplated bumping the Hoosiers up to No. 1 in the power rankings, but just couldn’t pull the trigger on putting a one-loss team above an undefeated one.

1. UCLA Bruins: 10-0, Def. Illinois, 22-14, Last Week: 1

UCLA didn’t play its cleanest game of the season on Friday night, but still got the job done in the rain against a stubborn Illinois team. The Bruins have likely locked up a CFP spot, as even if they lost out, a two-loss Big Ten team is making the playoff field.

michigan.headline: Trey McKenney embracing leadership role as a sophomore for Michigan
michigan.body:
Nov 6, 2026; Boston, Massachusetts, USA; Michigan Wolverines guard Trey McKenney (1) looks to shoot the ball against the UConn Huskies during the first half at TD Garden. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

Trey McKenney is one of the hardest working athletes in Ann Arbor.

Before his freshman season with the Wolverines, McKenney dropped 18 pounds in prepartion for the season, thanks to working out incredibly hard and changing his diet. As Tony Garcia detailed for The Detroit Free Press recently ($), Michigan had to temporarily cut off his keycard access to the Player Development Center after he tried to get shots up a few days after Michigan won the National Championship in April.

After being a key piece off the bench last season (9.9 points, 2.8 rebounds, 0.9 assists, 46.2 percent from the field, 39.1 percent from three), the former Michigan Mr. Basketball from Flint is stepping into a star role on Michigan’s 2026-27 squad. He received the key to his home city and brought the national title to the celebration this offseason, a sweet honor he previously talked about.

“It was amazing. Being from Flint and being able to celebrate a National Championship in my home state was pretty cool,” McKenney said. “Having all my family there and people that I knew growing up, it’s just something that I’m very proud of.”

McKenney has been asked to do more as a sophomore, starting at the 2 and being asked to be one of the main shot creators. He had a good game in Sunday’s win over William & Mary, scoring 14 points, grabbing five rebounds and dishing out five assists, but he wasn’t happy with his efficiency. He’s gotten off to a slower start on the year (22-of-56, 39.3 percent from the field) and has looked like he is forcing deep threes at times. But he’s still working on getting better shots for himself and his teammates.

“I feel like I’m getting more comfortable with the role,” McKenney said. “Obviously, the last four games, I haven’t been as efficient as I really want to be, but I feel like my efficiency is going to come throughout the season and I’ll get more comfortable in this role. I’ll be fine.”

As head coach Mike Boynton Jr. highlighted in his postgame availability, McKenney is now at the front of the scouting report. The first-year head coach said the coaches need to find more ways to get McKenney open, but it is still a work in progress.

“I love that he’s willing to be able to look himself in the mirror and figure out how he can be better. I think as a staff, we have to find ways to get him (more) free so the game is a little easier for him,” Boynton said. “There’s no doubt that he’s at the top of people’s scouting reports now as opposed to kind of an after-thought, a player who’s really good but you couldn’t pay a whole lot of attention to with the other guys that you had to really focus on.

“That means he’s got to find other ways, being a cutter, being a screener, thinking more about playmaking first as opposed as being aggressive to looking to score, because teams will try to take away his shot. The more games he plays and finds success, he had the over-the-top pass to Moustapha (Thiam), little plays like that over the course of the season will allow him to be more efficient when he is looking for his shot.”

McKenney was as crucial as Michigan’s coaching staff when it came to retaining the roster once Dusty May left. He was arguably Michigan’s best player during the overseas trip in August, and Boynton has said he will be counted on to create more shots this season. He has also stepped up as a leader — he’s always spoken softly, but McKenney has had to speak up more in his second season in Ann Arbor.

“I’ve definitely had to be more vocal in this leadership role,” McKenney said. “It’s part of my growth and it’s something that I’m going to have to get better at throughout the season. But I think I’ve done a pretty good job of motivating the guys, trying to let them know that we have to play to our standard and play Michigan basketball.”

As McKenney said, it will take time for him to get used to his role, but it feels like he’s one big performance away from putting the national college basketball media on notice. We’ve seen Michigan guards like Nik Stauskas and Kobe Bufkin make incredible sophomore leaps at Michigan. If McKenney makes a similar leap, another deep NCAA Tournament feels inevitable for the Wolverines.

michigan.headline: What we learned after Michigan Football’s loss to Oregon: There’s no foundation
michigan.body:
EUGENE, OR - NOVEMBER 14: Bryce Underwood #19 of the Michigan Wolverines passes the ball during the 2nd half of a game between the Michigan Wolverines and Oregon Ducks at Autzen Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Eugene, Oregon. (Photo by Al Sermeno/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images

As the Michigan Wolverines trotted off the field following a 31-7 loss to the Oregon Ducks, it was hard to consider how things could get much worse. New offensive play caller Jim Harding told the Michigan pregame radio that he shared with the staff that he “needs help.” Meanwhile, his message to the players was that they needed to “breathe life into the plays.”

The result? Quarterbacks that went 6-for-20 as they bounced in and out of game and 286 total yards of offense, two turnovers, and seven measly points. But it wasn’t just on the offensive end; Oregon jumped to a 14-point lead and never looked back. Against a team the Wolverines should annually compete with for the Big Ten crown, they were manhandled from start to finish in the latest example that this team has nothing left.

What we learned: Michigan has squandered two young QBs

The mismanagement of the quarterback room by this coaching staff has been dumbfounding. For a head coach like Kyle Whittingham to have decades of experience in this game, he has to understand the cultural dynamics of a quarterback change. As Michigan went from Bryce Underwood to Tommy Carr, there was newfound hope, despite growing pains that were expected from a true freshman quarterback.

What that meant was a world of pressure on Carr, the legacy name that was taking over for a five-star making millions. Instead of his head coaching continuing to give him votes of confidence, here’s how Whittingham handled the new quarterback battle following the comeback since the loss to Minnesota:

After Minnesota loss: “Jason [Beck] will call plays, and Bryce is our guy, and we move forward.”

After Penn State win: Whittingham said, “I’m not gonna say I was against (the move from Underwood to Carr) but they said, ‘Hey, thinking about making changes’… I’m not sitting here making a decision going forward who it’s gonna be because it was not just Bryce Underwood in the first half that wasn’t playing at the top of their game.”

Heading into the Indiana game: “We know exactly what we’re doing… The plan going forward, we’re not going to tip our hand to to the opponent, but we have a good plan in place, and that’s about all I can say on that right now.”

After loss to Indiana: Whittingham was asked point-blank who the starter was. His answer: “That’s to be determined. We don’t want to play this game every week, who’s going to start. But it’s a decision that we’ll make in the next couple days, keep it to ourselves until somebody lets the cat out of the bag, and go from there.”

Following the Rutgers win: “Liked everything about what (Carr) did,” said Whittingham, saying Carr will start for “the foreseeable future.”

Finally after the loss to Michigan State: Whittingham immediately gives up on Carr, saying the starting role is “to be determined” and that they thought about reinserting Underwood against the Spartans to “try and create something.” While saying they’d, “take a look at everything again and see what gives us the best chance to win.”

In Saturday’s loss to Oregon, Carr started, but Underwood played the second quarter. Then, Carr came back out to start the second half until Underwood returned at the end of the game. In the four games Carr has started, he got ONE vote of confidence from his head coach in the media, where he made it sound like his position was solid. As soon as he started to struggle against Michigan State, the first real adversity he faced behind a broken offensive line and an abysmal play caller, they were ALREADY having conversations about going back to Underwood? The foreseeable future Whittingham mentioned after Rutgers lasted five quarters. It’s indefensible.

Culturally, who is the leader of this offense? When it’s not the coaches, that’s what confidence in a quarterback affords even in the worst of moments. Teammates play hard for the guy who takes the most weight on offense. That’s typically the signal caller, and it’s why it is the most important position in sports. There was energy and momentum on this team when Carr took over. You could see it on the field as he made plays, but players in the locker room were raving each week about his work ethic and will to win. But, in the first game since firing Beck, this coaching staff decided to pull the plug on Carr after one quarter.

I’m not saying Carr was playing well. But these are the punches you role with when you make the decision to go to a freshman. Let him earn his scars, gain experience, and be ready to compete for a job the following season with a locker room that is hopefully behind him.

Instead, the coaches threw Carr into the deep end. This is a young man the coaches said had the “it factor” and was a “natural born leader” before the season. They looked at a resume that constituted of less than a month’s worth of football that was filled with drama on and off the field and still decided to go back to Underwood. Think of the message that sends to these two student athletes, the fans and the locker room — there’s absolutely nothing to build on here.

The handling of this situation is a microcosm of the complete ineptitude and lack of care this coaching staff continues to display. They have no long-term planning. They put their foot in their mouth week after week. They show zero investment in any player on this roster and create far more problems than they solve, all while driving this program into the ground.
